key_insight: Predicting time increments with a Fourier Neural Operator improves Rayleigh-Bénard convection forecasting accuracy over a standard full-state FNO baseline.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a compact, fast CFD surrogate suitable for accelerating 2D convection simulations while preserving benchmark-level accuracy.
method: Use a Fourier Neural Operator for 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection.
Predict time increments rather than complete flow states.
Keep the surrogate lightweight: 314k parameters and 1.26 MB, with 7 ms inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports higher accuracy than the standard FNO baseline and similar accuracy to previous benchmarks, while also noting generalization to finer meshes.
watch_item: Accuracy is still constrained by the resolution of the training data, so mesh refinement alone may not improve prediction quality.
paper_title: Fourier Neural Operators for Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
